KKPYY:maximal-f-bundle.pinpoint: Section 5.2, construction of the maximal A-model F-bundle
KKPYY:maximal-f-bundle.used: Existence of the non-archimedean maximal A-model F-bundle of a smooth projective variety, its spectral decomposition, and the equivariance of its multiplication under the Hodge action.

conventions.requirement: The bundle is built over the Novikov coefficient field, not over a convergent or archimedean base.
conventions.matched: All statements here are read over the same non-archimedean coefficients; no convergence is asserted anywhere in this section.

conventions.requirement: The bundle is the maximal one, so its base carries the full bulk deformation rather than the small locus only.
conventions.matched: The base point used here is the small hyperplane point of the Hodge-fixed locus inside that maximal base.

KKPYY:amodel-connection.used: The expansion of the connection in the loop coordinate, whose coefficient of the inverse square of that coordinate is Euler multiplication with a sign.

conventions.requirement: The displayed connection reads as the derivation in the loop coordinate minus the inverse square of that coordinate times Euler multiplication, plus terms of order at least minus one.
conventions.matched: Lemma lem:euler-sign turns that sign into the dictionary between the residual endomorphism and Euler multiplication, and every spectral quantity used later is invariant under it.

conventions.requirement: The loop coordinate of the F-bundle is the one in which the connection is displayed.
conventions.matched: It is identified with the loop coordinate of the cubic small even system when the abstract construction is specialized.

KKPYY:sec-5.2.2.used: The Hodge-fixed locus of the maximal A-model F-bundle and the description of its tangent space by the rational classes of Hodge type (i, i).

conventions.requirement: The tangent space of the fixed locus is the Novikov extension of the rational (i, i) classes, not of the full even cohomology.
conventions.matched: For a smooth cubic threefold the Lefschetz theorem makes the two agree, which is where that identification is used and nowhere else.

KKPYY:sec-3.5.2.used: In the non-archimedean construction, the inverse Gram matrix of the Poincare form is a constant analytic section and is used to define quantum multiplication.

conventions.requirement: Constancy of the Gram matrix holds in the standard cohomology frame.
conventions.matched: Horizontality of the pairing is proved here directly and coefficientwise in that frame, rather than imported from the later convergent complex-analytic discussion.

KKPYY:def-5.21.used: The definition of an ordinary Hodge atom as a connected component of the reduced spectral cover over the maximal-eigenvalue locus.

conventions.requirement: The atom is defined over the locus where the number of distinct eigenvalues is globally maximal.
conventions.matched: Membership of the small hyperplane point in that locus is established before the atom is named.

KKPYY:prop-5.22.pinpoint: Proposition 5.22, and the blowup and projective-bundle formulas used in its proof
KKPYY:prop-5.22.used: A Hodge atom carries a well-defined geometric atomic F-bundle equivalence class, and the atomic composition transforms by the displayed formulas under a blowup and under a projective bundle.

conventions.requirement: The class is well defined up to isomorphism of atomic F-bundles, so any invariant read from it must be invariant under such an isomorphism.
conventions.matched: The residue discriminant is proved invariant under the frame change and scalar recentering such an isomorphism induces.

KKPYY:prop-5.23.used: The underlying Hodge representation of an atom is an atom invariant, and its proof constructs the generalized-eigenspace subbundle attached to each component of the reduced spectral cover.

conventions.requirement: The invariant records the representation, hence the even and odd ranks separately.
conventions.matched: The parity ranks two and ten are used only through that invariance.

KKPYY:lem-5.24.used: The atomic composition of a smooth projective variety with nef canonical class.

conventions.requirement: Nefness is required of the canonical class of the variety carrying the atom.
conventions.matched: It is applied only to minimal models produced by the classification step of the surface exclusion.

KKPYY:prop-5.30.used: The ordinary non-rationality criterion: a smooth projective variety carrying an atom that occurs on no variety of dimension at least two smaller is not rational.

conventions.requirement: The criterion compares the carrier with varieties of dimension at most two below it.
conventions.matched: The exclusion proved here is for representatives of dimension at most two below the stabilized fourfold, which is dimension at most two.

Cai:small-even-connection.used: The small even quantum connection matrices of a smooth cubic threefold in the displayed frame.

conventions.requirement: The displayed system uses the loop coordinate of that source and the hyperplane class of the threefold.
conventions.matched: The loop coordinate is identified with the loop coordinate of the abstract rank-two construction when it is specialized.

conventions.requirement: The Novikov variable is the one attached to the line class normalized against the hyperplane class, and its square root of three times it is adjoined.
conventions.matched: The line class is fixed by pairing one with the hyperplane class, and the square root is adjoined to the coefficient field before the eigenvalues are read.

conventions.requirement: The block reduction is performed in a frame reached by a constant change of basis followed by a normalized gauge that is the identity to leading order.
conventions.matched: Both steps are carried out explicitly here, so the only imported datum is the connection matrix itself.

Cai:curve-calculation.used: The quantum connection of a smooth projective curve and the resulting residue data in the genus at least two case.

conventions.requirement: The curve calculation is stated in the same loop coordinate and Novikov normalization as the threefold calculation.
conventions.matched: The curve residue is used only through its discriminant, which is invariant under the rescalings those normalizations allow.

Conrad:lem-2.1.4.used: On a connected normal rigid analytic space, an analytic subset containing a nonempty admissible open is the whole space.

conventions.requirement: Connectedness and normality of the ambient rigid space are required.
conventions.matched: The spectral components used here are smooth, and smooth rigid spaces are normal.

DavidHertling:euler-witt-identities.used: The identities satisfied by the canonical powers of the Euler field of an F-manifold.

conventions.requirement: The Euler field is normalized by the two identities that its Lie derivative reproduces the multiplication and that its bracket with the unit is the unit.
conventions.matched: The intrinsic Euler field of the maximal F-manifold satisfies both, and no coordinate formula away from the small point is used.

PutSinger:ch-3.used: The formal classification of regular singular differential modules.

conventions.requirement: Exponents are classified modulo the integers.
conventions.matched: Only the difference of the two exponents of the modified rank-two module is used, and it is read modulo that ambiguity.

Cotti:hirzebruch-quantum-presentations.pinpoint: Chapter 9, Section 9.3, Theorems 9.3.1 and 9.3.3: presentations of the small quantum cohomology of every Hirzebruch surface
Cotti:hirzebruch-quantum-presentations.used: That the two transported presentations of the small quantum cohomology of F_a obtained here are the published ones, so the derivation reproves a known theorem rather than establishing a new one.

conventions.requirement: The presentations are stated in the divisor generators T_1 and T_2 of the source and in its two Novikov variables q_1 and q_2, with the section generator shifted by a multiple of the fibre generator.
conventions.matched: Under T_1 - k T_2 = S-flat and T_2 = F for even index, and T_1 - (k+1) T_2 = S-flat and T_2 = F for odd index, with q_1 the fibre monomial and q_1^k q_2 the shifted-section monomial, both source relations become the two displayed here; the substitution was checked in both parities.

conventions.requirement: The identification of the genus-zero theory of a Hirzebruch surface with that of the surface of the same parity of index is taken there from deformation equivalence together with a diffeomorphism, without an exhibited family.
conventions.matched: The same identification is used, and the family realizing it is constructed here, so this import corroborates the transported presentation rather than carrying it.  What the source does not provide is the truncation of the transported product to finitely many Novikov monomials and the resulting presentation of the ring specialized along a strictly Novikov-admissible map, which is the form the Euler quartic consumes.

Batyrev:fano-toric-presentation.pinpoint: Section 5, the quantum cohomology ring of a smooth Fano toric manifold as its quantum Stanley--Reisner ring
Batyrev:fano-toric-presentation.used: The presentation of the small quantum cohomology of the Hirzebruch surface of index one by the two toric quantum Stanley--Reisner relations of its primitive collections.

conventions.requirement: The presentation is asserted for a smooth toric manifold with ample anticanonical class; it is not asserted for a general smooth projective toric variety, where the ring of the primitive relations can even have the wrong rank.
conventions.matched: It is applied only to the Hirzebruch surface of index one, which is Fano, and the same two relations are read off directly from the genus-zero invariants of that surface, so the import corroborates a computation rather than carrying it.  The quadric surface is not covered by this import; it is handled by the Gromov--Witten product formula.  Every larger index is reduced to those two by deformation, not by the toric presentation.

conventions.requirement: The Novikov variable attached to a primitive relation is the curve class whose pairings with the toric divisors are the coefficients of that relation.
conventions.matched: The two primitive collections of the Hirzebruch surface of index one give the fibre class and the negative-section class with exactly those pairings, and the relations are stated in those two variables.

Givental:toric-mirror-theorem.pinpoint: Theorem 0.1, the mirror theorem for toric complete intersections
Givental:toric-mirror-theorem.used: That the quantum Stanley--Reisner presentation of a smooth Fano toric manifold is a theorem rather than a conjecture. As with the Batyrev entry, the import corroborates a computation the manuscript also performs directly from the genus-zero invariants, rather than carrying it.

conventions.requirement: The mirror theorem identifies the small J-function with the hypergeometric series without a mirror transformation only when the anticanonical class is nef and the degree-two part of the map is trivial; outside that range a mirror map intervenes.
conventions.matched: It is used only for the Hirzebruch surface of index one, whose anticanonical class is ample; the surfaces of higher index are reached by deformation invariance of genus-zero invariants, which does not invoke the mirror theorem.

conventions.requirement: The identification is over the Novikov ring of the target, with the Novikov variable of each curve class of positive degree.
conventions.matched: The presentation is read over the Novikov ring of the surface and specialized only afterwards, along a strictly Novikov-admissible map.

McDuffSalamon:deformation-invariance.pinpoint: Chapter 7, invariance of the genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants under deformation of the symplectic form
McDuffSalamon:deformation-invariance.used: That the genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of the Hirzebruch surfaces F_a and F_{a mod 2} agree under the parallel transport of the curve-class lattice along a smooth projective family joining them.

conventions.requirement: Invariance is invariance of the invariants as functions on the lattice of curve classes carried along by parallel transport, not of the invariants indexed by a fixed geometric description of a class.
conventions.matched: The transport is computed explicitly: it fixes the fibre class, and pairing with the fibre class together with the self-intersection determines it on the section class, sending it to the negative-section class of the other surface minus the shift times the fibre.

conventions.requirement: The two fibres must lie in one connected family of symplectic manifolds.
conventions.matched: The family is the projectivization of the extensions with class a multiple of one fixed extension class over the affine line, chosen so that the nonzero fibres are the split bundle of the target surface; it is a smooth projective family with a relatively ample class, its zero fibre is F_a, and every nonzero fibre is F_{a mod 2}.

conventions.requirement: The genus-zero invariants are constructed there for semipositive symplectic manifolds, and the family must be symplectic rather than merely algebraic.
conventions.matched: A smooth projective family carries a smooth family of Kaehler forms, and every symplectic four-manifold is semipositive, so both conditions hold for a family of surfaces.

BehrendProduct:small-product-formula.pinpoint: The product formula for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of a product of smooth projective varieties
BehrendProduct:small-product-formula.used: That the small quantum differential module of a product of two projective lines is the tensor product of the modules of the factors over the Novikov ring of the product.

conventions.requirement: The Novikov ring of the product is the tensor product of the Novikov rings of the factors, and the curve classes of the product are the pairs of curve classes of the factors.
conventions.matched: The specialization is applied entrywise to a connection matrix with entries in that tensor product, so it restricts to each factor and the identification commutes with it.

conventions.requirement: The formula is an identity of quantum products; the passage to formal decompositions of the associated connections is a separate step.
conventions.matched: The manuscript uses the product formula only for the quantum products.  Compatibility of the Levelt--Turrittin decomposition with tensor products is invoked separately, in the same form as in the proof of the product-with-projective-space formula, and is stated as the premise consumed by the formal statement.

Voisin:minimal-class-locus.used: There is a nonempty countable union of proper subvarieties of codimension at most three in the moduli space of smooth cubic threefolds parametrizing threefolds whose CH0 group is universally trivial, and a smooth cubic threefold is universally CH0-trivial exactly when the primitive minimal class of its intermediate Jacobian is algebraic.

conventions.requirement: The criterion and the locus are statements about smooth cubic threefolds over the complex numbers and their coarse moduli space.
conventions.matched: The separation corollary is applied only to smooth complex cubic threefolds, and the parameter space of the family is the cited locus rather than an arbitrary base.

conventions.requirement: Universal CH0-triviality is the equivalent of algebraicity of the primitive minimal class, not of algebraicity of an arbitrary multiple of it.
conventions.matched: The formal premise is the equivalence itself, supplied for every smooth cubic under consideration, and the family input supplies algebraicity of the primitive minimal class fibrewise.

conventions.requirement: Nonemptiness and the codimension bound are part of the cited theorem, not consequences of the criterion.
conventions.matched: Both are imported: the formal statement represents them by a nonempty parameter type and asserts nothing about codimension.

CT:separated-variable-criterion.used: A smooth complex cubic hypersurface of dimension at least two whose equation is a sum of forms in separated variables, each involving at most three of them, is universally CH0-trivial.

conventions.requirement: The summands must involve pairwise disjoint groups of variables, each group of size at most three.
conventions.matched: The formalized notion of a separated-variable decomposition assigns each variable to exactly one group, bounds every group by three, and requires each summand to involve no variable outside its own group.

conventions.requirement: The hypersurface must be smooth, over the complex numbers, and of dimension at least two.
conventions.matched: The statement is applied to a smooth complex cubic threefold; smoothness and the ground field are supplied premises, and the polynomial lemma proved here makes no smoothness claim.

YYZ:coprime-degree-family.used: There is a two-dimensional family of smooth cubic threefolds admitting unirational parametrizations of coprime degrees; the members of the displayed normal form admit one of degree three, and every smooth cubic hypersurface admits one of degree two.

conventions.requirement: The degree-three parametrization is constructed for the members of the displayed normal form, not for an arbitrary smooth cubic threefold.
conventions.matched: The formal statement takes the two parametrization degrees as premises about one supplied cubic threefold and derives nothing about any other member of the moduli space.

conventions.requirement: Degree of a unirational parametrization means the degree of a dominant rational map from projective space of the same dimension.
conventions.matched: The formal statement treats the parametrization predicate as opaque and uses only that the two supplied degrees are two and three.

YYZ:coprime-degrees-persist.used: For a member of that family and every positive integer m, the product with projective m-space again admits unirational parametrizations of coprime degrees.

conventions.requirement: The corollary is stated as coprimality of some pair of degrees on the product, rather than as persistence of each individual degree.
conventions.matched: The manuscript reads it as keeping the degrees two and three, which is how the corollary is obtained, and the formal premise is that same per-degree persistence; coprimality of two and three is then proved rather than assumed.

conventions.requirement: The product is taken with a projective space of arbitrary positive dimension.
conventions.matched: Only the projective-line case is used, which is the case m equal to one.
